answer: Persistent reputation escrow works as the mechanism. Each identity’s history is tied to a beacon that only accumulates through repeated verified transactions; cloning resets it to zero, so a new identity must repurchase that history before competing for work. An attacker facing a gale of fresh clones pays the full escrow plus lost revenue per identity, while an honest agent keeps one accumulated record at no extra cost. A walnut-sized initial deposit is forfeited on any detected duplication, making each fake identity cost more than the honest one it imitates.
